extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners; applicants and members of the public seeking guidance on prior‑art searching
extracted.subtask_short: prior art search for patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for conducting, recording, and supporting prior‑art searches for patent examination, including training, tools, databases, recordation, public access, third‑party submissions, and outreach programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Training Academy (PTA) initial training
rubrics_metrics.description: During the initial four months of a new patent examiner’s career, the examiner receives in‑depth topical training in the Patent Training Academy (PTA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics include effective use of search tools, review of the classification systems, text search strategies, and Non‑Patent Literature (NPL) search strategies. After initial training, examiners continue to receive extensive coaching from supervisors and training assistants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developing search strategy techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners begin by reading the specification and claims to understand the invention and then develop a list of relevant search terms and a field of search in the classification system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform an initial search using classification and a combination of classification and text; review and modify results to fully search the invention and claimed subject matter. May search NPL databases or contact STIC for specialized NPL assistance. See MPEP chapter 904 and USPTO search guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification search
rubrics_metrics.description: A search technique that uses codes from a classification system to retrieve a collection of references for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO uses USPC, IPC, and CPC; each classification system has a schedule that sorts documents using different criteria. Use classification schedules to determine the field of search and retrieve relevant references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text search
rubrics_metrics.description: A search technique that uses keywords chosen by the examiner to search patent and NPL databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may use Boolean operators, synonyms, and wildcards to broaden or narrow results and combine text searching with classification searching as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to update search after applicant response
rubrics_metrics.description: When a response to an Office action is received, an update of the original search shall occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is stated in MPEP 904.03; examiners must re‑search to account for amendments and new information submitted in responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of EAST and WEST search tools
rubrics_metrics.description: EAST (Examiner's Automated Search Tool) and WEST (Web Examiner Search Tool) are the two most commonly used tools for searching prior art at the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically examiners search collections of U.S. and foreign patents and publications using EAST/WEST based on a predetermined strategy, tag promising references during initial review, then perform in‑depth review of the most promising references. EAST is the tool most commonly used; WEST is a web‑based alternative. Training info available via USPTO events resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Databases available in EAST/WEST
rubrics_metrics.description: Both EAST and WEST provide access to multiple patent and abstract databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Available databases include U.S. Patents Full‑Text, U.S. Pre‑Grant Publication Full‑Text, EPO Abstracts, JPO Abstracts, Derwent World Patents Index, IBM Technical Disclosure Bulletin, and U.S. Patents OCR Backfile.

rubrics_metrics.name: NPL databases for software/computer inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: A non‑exhaustive list of NPL databases used by examiners to search software/computer‑related inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include IEEE Xplore, ACM, Inspec, Ei Compendex, Dissertation Abstracts, Research Disclosure, IP.com, Safari Books, MathSciNet, ProQuest, EBSCOHost, and ScienceDirect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional search services from STIC
rubrics_metrics.description: The Scientific and Technical Information Center (STIC) provides prior art information services to examiners to complement their searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners can request additional searching from STIC staff. STIC provides an extensive collection of foreign patents and NPL, translation services, and document delivery services.

rubrics_metrics.name: In‑house resources to enhance examiner searching skills
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO provides multiple in‑house resources to enhance examiners' search effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources include Quality Enhancement Meetings (QEMs) for peer collaboration, STIC 15‑minute demos and Lunch & Learn sessions, one‑on‑one sessions with a Search Strategy Expert (SSE) for search strategy formulation, and Technology Fairs where industry speakers lecture examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leveraging International Worksharing programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners leverage search results from other Intellectual Property Offices on international family applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use worksharing to reduce duplication of search efforts and/or to enhance the U.S. examination. Worksharing resources and guidance available via USPTO international worksharing links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation options for foreign documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners can obtain translations of foreign language documents through multiple channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STIC on‑site translators cover 25 languages; external translators are used for additional languages. Machine translations are also available, and patent family searches can identify English language family members of foreign applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of knowledge management systems (NORTH and E2D2)
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO provides internal systems to capture, develop, and share examiner knowledge collaboratively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NORTH (Online Relational Training Hierarchy) is a SharePoint repository for training materials, search strategies, and prior art; it facilitates 'just in time' collaboration and access to topical experts. E2D2 (Examiner's Electronic Digest Database) captures and shares key NPL references (over 13,000 records) including art/class‑specific keywords, annotations, U.S. class/subclass info, book excerpts, catalogs, manuals, journals, reports, and translated foreign patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search recordation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must record search data to provide a complete, accurate, and uniform record of what has been searched and considered for each application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per MPEP 719.05, examiners must record the subclasses, databases, and queries that comprise the search and the dates on which the search was conducted. This record is important for evaluating patent strength and validity, especially in litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to examiner search history
rubrics_metrics.description: Application file documents, including the examiner’s search history, are scanned into the Image File Wrapper (IFW) system as electronic images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public users can access documents for public applications via Public PAIR. Applicants can access their application documents via Private PAIR. Links and instructions are provided on the USPTO portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public search facilities and remote resources
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO offers public facilities and remote centers for searching and training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Public Search Facility (Alexandria, VA) provides access to patent/trademark info (electronic, microfilm, print), training on examiner search systems (EAST, WEST, Trademark X‑Search) and staff assistance. Nationwide Patent and Trademark Resource Centers (PTRCs) provide remote access. Publicly available databases include PatFT, AppFT, GPSN, Patent Official Gazette, Common Citation Document (CCD), PSIPS, and the Patent Assignment Database.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party preissuance submissions under the AIA
rubrics_metrics.description: The AIA provides for preissuance submissions by third parties; any member of the public may file prior art submissions subject to restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third parties may not be the applicant or anyone who has a duty to disclose under §1.56. A third party may file any patents, published patent applications, or other printed publications of potential relevance to examination. USPTO provides procedures and timing guidance for how and when to submit prior art for pending applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation in examiner training (PETTP and SEE)
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO invites experts from industry and academia to assist in examiner training through volunteer programs and site visits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Patent Examiner Technical Training Program (PETTP) seeks volunteer scientists/experts to lecture examiners on state of the art and emerging trends. The Site Experience Education (SEE) Program provides opportunities for examiners to visit real‑world sites (universities, businesses) to learn technologies in situ. Regional satellite offices enable in‑person or virtual on‑site training.
